transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

I can certainly help you with that stuttering issue on your Dyson vacuum. Since the battery is fully charged, this pulsing usually means the motor is detecting restricted airflow and protecting itself from overheating. To guide you to the correct fix or part, I need to know exactly which model you have. The model number is typically printed on a label on the body of the vacuum, often under the bin or near where the battery sits. If you can't find it right now, we can try some general checks first, but having that number helps me be precise.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a v8 animal, sv10 on the label. no burning smell or heat btw

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Thanks for confirming the model and noting there’s no heat or burning smell. Since the battery is full but it still stutters, this is very often caused by a blockage in the airway rather than a part failure. Please detach the wand and floorhead from the main body and look through each tube to ensure nothing like a coin or debris is stuck inside. Also check that the bin isn’t completely clogged at the inlet where it connects to the motor housing. Let me know if you find any blockages there, as clearing them often solves this pulsing issue immediately.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
found a big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom of the wand where the head goes on, pulled it out. bin inlet was a bit dusty so wiped it

That blockage removal was a great step, but since it’s still pulsing, we need to check the filters as they are the most common cause of this issue on Dyson models. Please remove both the pre-motor and post-motor (HEPA) filters from the top of the vacuum body; these can get clogged with fine dust that isn't visible at first glance. Wash them in cold water only—do not use soap or put them in a dishwasher—and let them dry completely for at least 24 hours in a warm room. It is crucial they are fully dry before you put them back, as even slightly damp filters will cause the motor to cut out immediately due to airflow restriction. Let me know once this is done and if the pulsing stops when you try it again on normal mode.
washed the filter, never done it in 3 yrs lol, water came out black. left it overnight on the radiator. pulses way less now but still a bit

That’s great progress with the filters, but since it still pulses occasionally, we need to check for any remaining blockages in the floorhead itself. Please detach the wand from the floorhead and look through the tube to ensure nothing like a coin or small debris is stuck inside the brush bar housing. You can also try turning the roller by hand with the vacuum switched off to make sure it isn't jammed by hair wrapped around the ends of the brush. If you find any blockages there, clear them out and let me know if that resolves the final bit of stuttering.
took the wand off already, thats where the clump was. its fine now, proper suction, no pulsin. brush bar had a bit of hair, cut it off

That is excellent news! I am glad we could get your Dyson V8 Animal back up and running with proper suction. To help stop this from happening again, try to check the brush bar for hair tangles every few weeks, as that is usually what causes these blockages in the first place. Is there anything else you need help with today?
